name: Burpee
summary: Squat, hands to the floor, jump the feet back to a plank, back in, and jump up.
setup: From standing, squat and put the hands down, jump the feet back to a plank (add a push-up if you like), jump them back in, and jump up with the arms overhead.
why: The body goes from standing to lying to jumping — the calibrated counter cannot follow it. Logged by hand.
dosage: 3 × 10, or as many as possible in a minute.
regression: Step the feet back and in; no jump.
contraindications: Wrist, shoulder, knee or back injury; anyone told to avoid impact.

faults.label: Hips sagging in the plank
faults.tip: The hips land level with the shoulders, not below.

faults.label: Back rounding on the way up
faults.tip: Land the feet wide enough to stand with the chest up.

faults.label: Hips sagging in the plank
faults.tip: The tired middle of a burpee set is where the back starts to sag.

faults.label: Landing hard
faults.tip: Absorb the jump. Loud landings are how the knees and ankles complain later.

guide.cannotSee: The whole thing — the calibrated pose is lost.
